criteria-objective.reason: ⚠️ RE-EVALUATED 2026-09-03 OVER 98 ACTIVE CRITERIA, counted from the graph rather than restated: 47 pass, 51 not-evaluated. The previous reason said 94, which was true when written; four more were authored for the setup transaction — ACC-0096, ACC-0097, ACC-0098, ACC-0099 — and ACC-0044 was evaluated. ⚠️ THE SWEEP FOR HARDCODED TOTALS REMAINS THE DURABLE PART of the last correction, and it is what caught this one: the count was recomputed because the graph moved, not because this record happened to be open for another reason. ⚠️ THE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE IN THIS PASS IS A SPLIT, NOT AN ADDITION. ACC-0043 and ACC-0045 are written against the setup COMMAND — every file it owns, the ignore block and the generated skills included, and an operator actually running the recorded resume command — and they were being carried by TSK-0026, which builds only the transaction primitive underneath. Two synthetic JSON files cannot evaluate either statement, so passing them there would have been an overclaim measured against the criterion's own words. Both now sit with TSK-0060, which composes the command; four new criteria state what the primitive itself guarantees. ⚠️ EACH OF THE FOUR NAMES AN OBSERVATION RATHER THAN A QUALITY, and each was written from the defect that would otherwise have passed it. ACC-0098 requires the file's MODIFICATION TIME to be unchanged, because a transaction can report 'no changes' while rewriting identical bytes. ACC-0097 requires a refused plan to leave no DIRECTORY behind and not merely no file — the defect behind it created `.pi/` and then refused, so the refusal still changed the project — and, after review, requires a cleanup that CANNOT complete to be a refusal naming every path left behind rather than a silent success. It also requires absence to be confirmed by observing the path: measured on Windows, `rmdir` against a file throws ENOENT and leaves the file where it was, so a criterion that accepted the error code as proof would have passed over a probe file still sitting in the project. ACC-0096 requires the refusal to rest on where a path RESOLVES, since a criterion satisfied by rejecting `../x` is also satisfied by the lexical check that let a junction through; it was WIDENED after review from location to identity, because a canonical location is not a canonical identity — `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/a/../settings.json` were both accepted as separate entries with separate recorded identities, and two overlapping authorized roots reach one file with keys that share no characters at all. ACC-0099 requires a failed journal deletion to be REPORTED, which is precisely the case a swallowed error hides behind a run that reports success. ⚠️ ACC-0044 is now pass and remains on BOTH TSK-0026 and TSK-0027: the transaction refuses a changed identity today, and TSK-0027 has to keep that true once the initializer runs inside a held transaction instead of taking its own lock. ⚠️ RE-CHECKED AFTER THE REVIEW REPAIRS: 98 active, 47 pass, 51 not-evaluated — ACC-0096 and ACC-0097 were WIDENED rather than added to, so that pass did not move the census. ⚠️ RE-COUNTED AGAIN FOR TSK-0027: 99 active, 49 pass, 50 not-evaluated, 5 approved and 94 draft. ACC-0100 is the one addition, and it exists because TSK-0027's only criterion was ACC-0044 — which states that the TRANSACTION refuses a changed identity, and says nothing about the initializer running inside a held one. A task marked accepted on a criterion that does not test it is the same overclaim ACC-0043 and ACC-0045 were, one task along. ACC-0044 stays on TSK-0027 as the regression it must not cause; ACC-0100 states what the task delivers, including the control that DISTINGUISHES nesting from concurrency — a guard that refused two concurrent initializers would have broken the exclusion it was added to protect. ⚠️ ACC-0100 WAS WIDENED TWICE BEFORE APPROVAL, and both times because a review reproduced something its statement did not cover: first the transaction's authenticated lifetime, then registration, quiescent drain, and the explicit NON-claim about already-settled promises. A criterion is objective only about what it names, so widening it was the work rather than a tidy-up. It is now approved. ⚠️ ACC-0077 WAS WIDENED FOR TSK-0055 from 'returns these fields, and is asserted to contain nothing sensitive' to the exact key set with every value compared to its source. The old wording was satisfiable by a scan for known-sensitive patterns, which passes on any field nobody thought to match, on a missing field, and on the two identifiers exchanged — three mutations that now fail. It also records where the guarantee actually comes from: every field of a success response is built from a validated value, so 'no absolute path in the response' holds by construction rather than by pattern-matching the output. That clause was WIDENED again after review, because the first version validated only the two identifiers and let an unreadable package version through as `build: null` in an otherwise complete 200 — four correct fields is exactly how a response that merely arrives gets past a reader checking that the fields are present. It now also requires the status, headers and parsed body to be observed over real HTTP, and the served identity to be proved to come from the RUNNING process by building with one identity and starting with another: the static check it replaced matched `/status,/`, which the route's own destructuring line already satisfied.
